output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Analysts still confirmed about 37 incidents in September and 36 in October, in line with the earlier average of about 38 a month. In those two months, 47 confirmed incidents were moved to the "Suspicious Activity – Monitoring" category, which the report doesn't count. Every change came from the Brackwater integration account. Each was made 3.5 hours after the case opened, just after the 4-hour containment-deadline warning fired, which removes the case from the containment-time and SLA figures. A script on a Brackwater analyst jump host did this. The connector wrote no category changes, so a platform fault is unlikely. None of the 47 has a containment record, so the 100% SLA figure and the bonus claim are unreliable. Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases and have the in-house team and Halvard verify containment on each. Remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Hold the renewal and bonus until Brackwater explains in writing. Don't invoice service credits until the contract position is checked. I'm unsure whether the dropped detection rules also cost us coverage, so check that separately. I'm confident in the main conclusion.
output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check on vendor-sourced reports, then competing-hypotheses weighing; two system records (X14 audit, X9 API log) collected.
